tool_summary: Manages launchd services and daemons on macOS: loading, unloading, starting, stopping, and enabling/disabling persistent agents and daemons. The functional equivalent of systemctl/service on Linux.
platform_notes: launchctl is macOS-specific. Modern subcommands (bootstrap, bootout, enable, disable, kickstart) supersede legacy load/unload/start/stop on recent macOS versions.

rules.description: The load/bootstrap subcommands register a launch agent or daemon plist, which can establish a process that runs automatically at login or boot, persisting beyond the current session. This is a common persistence mechanism.
rules.reversible_note: Reversible via unload/bootout, but the loaded agent may execute arbitrary code before being removed.

rules.description: The unload/bootout/stop subcommands immediately affect a running service's availability, which can disrupt dependent processes or connections.

Manages launchd services and daemons. The list/print subcommands enumerate every running daemon and agent with PIDs and labels, which reveals installed security tools, monitoring agents, and third-party software running as persistent services -- reconnaissance value useful for profiling a system before deciding how to evade detection.
